Every script follows a Multiple Hooks → Body → CTA structure engineered for watch time and keeps viewers past the 15-second mark through storytelling — not selling.

min reading

Most UGC ads lose viewers by second 3. The creative looks authentic, the creator is likeable, but the script has no structure — no reason to keep watching. The result: wasted spend and ROAS that never climbs past break-even.

High-ROAS UGC ads solve this with a specific script architecture: multiple hooks at the top, a body that earns attention through storytelling, and a CTA placed at peak engagement. Every element is engineered for watch time — because watch time is what platforms reward with cheaper distribution.

The problem isn't production quality or creator selection. It's script structure. Most brands hand creators a brief that says "talk about the product" — and the result is a 30-second monologue that viewers skip in 2 seconds. The ads that drive measurable ROAS share three structural elements:
Multiple hook variations tested per script — not one opening, but 3-4, each designed to stop a different segment of the audience
A body that uses storytelling (problem → discovery → result) instead of feature listing
CTAs placed at the moment of peak emotional engagement, not bolted onto the end
This is the script architecture OKAD Agency uses across every UGC ad project. It's not a creative philosophy — it's an engineering decision based on platform algorithms and viewer behavior data.

Hooks (first 1-3 seconds): Each script gets 3-4 hook variations. One might lead with a question ("I was spending $200/month on skincare until..."), another with a bold claim ("This replaced my entire morning routine"), another with a pattern interrupt (unexpected visual or sound). The hooks are modular — they can be swapped without reshooting the body of the ad. This means one production day generates dozens of testable combinations.

Body (seconds 3-20): The body earns the next 15 seconds through narrative structure, not product features. The viewer stays because they want to know what happened — not because they care about ingredients or specs. Storytelling formats that consistently outperform: personal transformation ("here's what changed"), unexpected discovery ("I wasn't looking for this but..."), and social proof narrative ("my friend told me to try this and I didn't believe her").

CTA (seconds 15-30): The CTA lands when the viewer is most invested in the story — typically right after the transformation reveal or the social proof payoff. "Link in bio" at peak engagement converts 3-5x better than the same CTA at the end of a flat product demo.

Longevity (supplements for men 40+, Europe-to-US market) faced a unique challenge: the product requires education. You can't sell longevity supplements with a 3-second hook and a discount code. The audience needs to understand why they should care — and that takes time. OKAD Agency built the entire creative testing framework from scratch, including what constitutes a test, A/B variation structure, winner identification criteria, and reporting templates. The scripts used a doctor-figure storytelling format — an authority character walking the viewer through the science in plain language, supported by AI-generated organ visualizations that made abstract health concepts tangible.

The result: 15+ second average watch time on paid ads — well past the critical mark where platforms start rewarding the creative with cheaper impressions. Multilingual content (DE, DK, EN) with educational storytelling proved that even complex, education-heavy products can hold attention when the script is built around narrative, not features.
VueSwiss (Swiss skincare) and InstaHeadshots (AI headshot generator) both operate at high creative volume — and both prove that the multiple-hooks model scales.

VueSwiss produces ~30 videos per day: 10+ base scripts, each with 3+ hook variations, sustaining stable order volume for 2-3 months running. The hooks aren't random — each variation targets a different audience segment or emotional trigger. One hook might lead with vanity ("your skin after 2 weeks"), another with skepticism ("I didn't believe Swiss skincare was worth the price"), another with social proof ("my dermatologist recommended this").

InstaHeadshots follows the same framework: 70 scripts across talking head, voiceover, and music+text formats — each with 3 distinct hook variations. The hooks are tested systematically: which opening drives the highest view-to-15-second retention, which converts to clicks, which produces the best CPA. The modular structure means creative testing velocity stays high without proportional increases in production cost.

Some products need more than a good script — they need editing that matches the energy of the hook. Lookalikey (AI photo app) and ZenToes (foot care, Walmart launch) both required creative where the editing itself became part of the hook.

For ZenToes, OKAD Agency produced 10 static and 10 video ads using a modular hook-testing framework — 3-4 different hooks per video, each designed to stop the scroll in a commodity category where every competitor's ad looks the same. The editing approach: fast cuts between before/after shots, dynamic text overlays that reveal information in sync with the voiceover, and visual transitions timed to keep the viewer's eye moving. The result: 8%+ view-to-25-second retention rates — a benchmark most DTC brands struggle to reach at 4%.

Lookalikey's ads combine the same hook-testing methodology with editing designed for the AI/tech audience: screen recordings, transformation reveals, and side-by-side comparisons that demonstrate the product in real time. The dynamic editing style — quick cuts, zoom-ins on details, split-screen before/after — keeps engagement high through visual storytelling rather than verbal explanation.

The connection between watch time and ROAS isn't philosophical — it's mechanical. Meta, TikTok, and YouTube all use watch time as a primary signal for ad quality scoring. Higher watch time = higher quality score = lower CPM = more impressions per dollar = better ROAS. The math is straightforward:
A 15-second ad with 80% completion rate gets dramatically cheaper distribution than a 15-second ad with 30% completion
Cheaper distribution means more impressions per dollar
More impressions at the same conversion rate = higher ROAS
The compounding effect: better watch time → cheaper CPMs → more data → faster optimization → even better ROAS

This is why script structure matters more than production quality. A well-structured UGC script shot on an iPhone will outperform a poorly structured studio ad every time — because the algorithm rewards the one people actually watch.
The metrics that matter for high-ROAS UGC campaigns:
View-to-15-second retention: The single most important leading indicator. If viewers aren't making it to second 15, the script structure needs work — not the creative polish.
Hook-through rate: What percentage of viewers make it past the first 3 seconds? Test this across all hook variations to identify winners.

CPA by hook variation: Different hooks attract different audience segments. Some hooks drive higher volume at higher CPA; others drive lower volume at lower CPA. The right choice depends on your scaling goals.
ROAS by creative: Track at the individual creative level, not the campaign level. One winning creative can carry an entire campaign — identify it fast and scale it.
Creative fatigue timeline: How many days before a winning creative's performance degrades? Plan your production calendar around this number.
High ROAS isn't a one-time win — it requires a production system that generates testable creative at consistent velocity. OKAD Agency's model:
626+ vetted UGC creators across niches — matched by audience, not just category
Modular script architecture — every script designed for 3-4 hook swaps without reshooting
48-72 hour turnaround from brief to deliverable
Systematic hook testing — data decides winners, not creative instinct
Cross-platform optimization — same base creative adapted for TikTok, Meta, and YouTube Shorts

This infrastructure powered ZenToes' Walmart launch (20 ad variations from one production cycle), VueSwiss' sustained ~30 videos/day output, and Longevity's multilingual testing framework — each proving that ROAS scales with creative velocity, not creative budget.
OKAD Agency specializes in high-ROAS UGC ad production with a script-first methodology:
UGC script writing with Multiple Hooks → Body → CTA architecture
Hook testing and creative strategy (3-4 hooks per script, modular swapping)
Storytelling-driven scripts engineered for 15+ second watch time
High-volume production: VueSwiss (~30 videos/day), InstaHeadshots (70 scripts with 3 hook variations each)
Dynamic editing for hook-driven formats (fast cuts, before/after reveals, split-screen)
Creator sourcing from 626+ vetted UGC creators
Cross-platform optimization for TikTok, Meta, and YouTube
Performance tracking: view-to-15s retention, hook-through rate, CPA by variation, ROAS by creative

A high-ROAS UGC ad combines strong watch time (driven by script structure, not production quality) with a CTA placed at peak engagement. The Multiple Hooks → Body → CTA framework consistently outperforms single-hook scripts because it allows systematic testing of which opening drives the best performance for each audience segment. OKAD Agency's campaigns achieve 8%+ view-to-25-second retention through this methodology.

Three to four hook variations per script is the standard for systematic testing. Fewer than three doesn't generate enough data to identify winners; more than four creates diminishing returns relative to production cost. VueSwiss runs 3+ hooks per base script across ~30 videos per day — proving the model scales.

Watch time directly affects your CPM. Platforms reward ads that hold attention with cheaper distribution — which means more impressions per dollar before a single click happens. A high-watch-time ad with a moderate CTR will outperform a low-watch-time ad with a high CTR on total ROAS, because the distribution cost advantage compounds across every impression.

The key is modular production: scripts designed so hooks can be swapped without reshooting, creators matched by audience segment, and systematic testing that lets data — not instinct — decide winners. OKAD Agency's model produces dozens of testable variations from each production cycle, keeping creative velocity high while controlling costs.

Discover how AI-generated videos and avatars are revolutionizing content creation. Learn how brands boost engagement, cut costs, and scale fast—without sacrificing quality. This guide reveals smart strategies to maximize impact and stay ahead in the AI-powered marketing era.
min reading
January 18, 2024

Artificial intelligence is now deeply integrated into our daily lives, influencing industries across the board. One of the most exciting applications of AI is content creation, where AI-generated videos are transforming brand development strategies.
In this article, we’ll explore how AI can be leveraged to create engaging video content, the advantages and limitations of AI avatars, and how brands can maximize their impact.

AI-generated content refers to text, images, videos, and other media created using AI-powered tools. These systems utilize machine learning and natural language processing to automate content creation while maintaining high quality.
Efficiency: AI speeds up content production, allowing brands to publish more frequently.
Cost Savings: No need for studios, professional models, or expensive equipment.
Scalability: AI-generated videos can be adapted for multiple platforms.
Consistency: AI ensures uniform brand messaging across different content pieces.
AI avatars are virtual human-like figures that can mimic speech and facial expressions, commonly used in video marketing, customer support, and branding.
✅ Faster content production – AI avatars eliminate the need for on-site filming.
✅ Lower costs – No need to hire actors, rent studios, or invest in filming equipment.
✅ Brand consistency – AI avatars maintain a unified brand identity.
❌ Limited emotional depth – AI avatars may lack natural facial expressions.
❌ Lower engagement – Viewers may connect more with real humans.
❌ Less authenticity – AI-generated content can feel robotic if not optimized correctly.
To enhance AI avatar videos, we implemented:
Dynamic stock videos in the background for added depth.
Subtitles and simple animations to maintain engagement.
Varied camera angles for a more natural feel.
🚀 Result: Increased watch time and user engagement.
Using AI avatars isn’t just about convenience—it’s a strategic investment. Brands and content creators benefit from:
Higher efficiency – More videos in less time.
Lower production costs – No need for traditional video shoots.
Scalability – Easily localize videos for different markets.
💡 Did You Know? AI-generated videos perform well in retargeting campaigns, improving ROI on social media ads.
We leveraged AI avatars in SPIRITME from scratch, without a budget for advertising. The results were impressive:
6,000+ views on YouTube
2,000+ maximum reach per clip on YouTube
2,000+ views on Instagram
2,000+ views on TikTok

No, AI is not a substitute for human creativity—but it is a powerful tool that enhances content production. AI helps streamline processes, reduce costs, and improve efficiency, making content creation more accessible to brands and creators.
AI enhances branding by ensuring consistency, increasing content output, and improving targeting capabilities through automation.
AI avatars are effective but lack the authenticity of real influencers. Many brands use a hybrid approach—AI for scalability and human creators for relatability.
Popular AI video tools include Synthesia, DeepBrain AI, and Runway ML for realistic avatars and AI-generated video editing.
By adding dynamic elements like motion graphics, subtitles, and interactive content, brands can make AI videos more engaging.

AI-generated content is a game-changer for brands looking to scale their video production. While AI avatars have limitations, strategic implementation enhances engagement and maximizes ROI. By embracing AI, brands can stay ahead in the fast-evolving digital landscape.

High-converting video ads are critical for direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands to stand out in a crowded digital marketplace. This article explores the key strategies, frameworks, and best practices for creating video ads that drive results.

Short-form video dominates DTC advertising, with platforms like TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts driving the highest engagement. Brands that embrace creator-led UGC (user-generated content) see significantly better performance than those relying solely on polished, studio-produced content.
Key trends include:
Creator-led UGC outperforming traditional polished ads
Story-driven content with emotional hooks
Shoppable video formats with in-app checkout
AI-powered personalization and first-party data targeting

Here's what happened when OKAD Agency applied these trends to a real DTC launch: ZenToes, a foot care brand, needed to break into Walmart's retail ecosystem with ads that would stand out in a commodity category. We produced 10 static and 10 video ads using a modular hook-testing framework — 3-4 different hooks per video, each designed to stop the scroll in a different way. The result: 8%+ view-to-25-second retention rates, a benchmark that most DTC brands struggle to reach even at 4%. This campaign became the template for how we approach every DTC video project.
DTC brands face several challenges in video advertising:
Ad fatigue from overexposure to similar content
Rising CPMs and increasing competition for attention
Platform algorithm changes affecting organic reach
Limited production budgets compared to legacy brands

When Dadadababy, a DTC baby furniture brand, came to OKAD Agency, they were drowning in these problems. Part of Sego, a 3rd-generation Israeli furniture manufacturer with cribs made in Italy and shipping from New Jersey, they sell across 6 channels: DTC, Amazon, Target, Babylist, Wayfair, and Bambi Baby. Their generic static ads blended into the feed, CPMs were climbing, and they had no systematic way to test what worked. Through research — reviews, purchase behavior, geographic data — we identified their core audience: New York City moms, design-conscious, high-income, living in apartments where every piece of furniture is a deliberate choice. We analyzed competitors: Nestig, Babyletto, Pottery Barn Kids. Our solution: AI-generated visuals under $700 vs $3,000-8,000 for a traditional shoot, combined with reworked UGC from real parents. One shoot produced 20-30 visual variations across all 6 sales channels. The AI statics provided visual novelty (pattern interrupt), while the UGC maintained the warmth and trust that parent audiences demand. The result was a 3x increase in CTR — proving that the right creative strategy can overcome every one of these challenges, even on a modest budget.
Effective DTC video ads follow proven storytelling structures:
Problem-Agitate-Solve (PAS): Identify a pain point, amplify it, then present your product as the solution
Before-After-Bridge: Show life before your product, after, and how your brand bridges the gap
Social Proof Loop: Lead with testimonials, demonstrate the product, close with a CTA

The first 3 seconds are critical — hooks must stop the scroll immediately. OKAD Agency's ZenToes campaign for Walmart is the gold standard here: we produced modular hook variations — swapping opening lines, visuals, and CTAs — specifically to find the combinations that stopped thumbs. This systematic hook testing is what separates high-performing DTC ads from average ones.
Brands that tap into cultural moments and trending audio see dramatically higher engagement. TikTok's algorithm rewards content that feels native to the platform, not repurposed TV commercials.

OKAD Agency's organic UGC campaigns prove this principle with hard numbers. For YourChristianDate (Dating.com Group), we built a full-cycle organic content system that generated 1M+ organic views — no paid traffic. The target was 60 videos per month with +15% monthly growth. The biggest breakthrough: observational, first-timer humor worked; preachy and authority-based formats bombed. Two creator archetypes resonated most: a younger attractive male creator and a confident, charismatic man around 50 — both US-based. For Skribly (drawing app), we produced 1,257 videos across 2 creators, 4 accounts, and 3 platforms — resulting in 1.5M views and 2,000 registrations. For Twinsfit (sportswear), 54 Reels generated 127K views from just 485 followers with a 6.12% engagement rate. For Godka (premium alcohol), individual posts hit 200K, 300K, 600K, 700K, and 900K views — all from content produced during a single production day in Lisbon with a professional bartender on set. These aren't outliers — they're the result of deliberately building content around cultural relevance rather than brand messaging.
Mobile-first vertical formats (9:16 ratio)
Bold text overlays and captions (85% of social video watched without sound)
Fast-paced editing with cuts every 2-3 seconds
Authentic, lo-fi aesthetic outperforms high-production in many categories
Each platform requires different specifications:
TikTok: 9:16, 1080x1920, 15-60 seconds, native audio trends
Instagram Reels: 9:16, up to 90 seconds, strong hook in first frame
YouTube Shorts: 9:16, under 60 seconds, SEO-optimized titles
Facebook/Meta: Square (1:1) or vertical, longer form allowed
High-converting CTAs are:
Specific and action-oriented ("Shop Now," "Get 20% Off Today")
Placed at peak engagement moments, not just at the end
Tested across multiple variations for optimization
Successful DTC brands treat video ads as experiments:
Test multiple hooks for the same creative concept
Run A/B tests on CTAs, music, and voiceovers
Analyze view-through rates, CTR, and ROAS to identify winners
Scale winning creatives and iterate on losers

For Dadadababy (baby furniture, part of Sego), OKAD Agency's iterative approach tells the whole story. We tested AI static ads — produced under $700 vs $3,000-8,000 for a traditional shoot — against reworked UGC from real parents. Multiple visual directions running simultaneously against the same audiences, deployed across 6 sales channels (DTC, Amazon, Target, Babylist, Wayfair, Bambi Baby). The data was unambiguous: AI-generated visuals drove 3x higher CTR than the original creative, with 20-30 visual variations from one shoot. But the insight went deeper — it was the combination of AI novelty + UGC authenticity that created a compound effect. That insight allowed the brand to scale confidently, knowing exactly which creative formula worked and why.

For Longevity (supplements for men 40+, Europe to US), OKAD Agency built the entire creative testing framework from scratch: what constitutes a test, A/B variations, winner identification, reporting templates. First test: €917 spend, 5 purchases, CPA €183. Multilingual content (DE, DK, EN) with educational storytelling featuring a doctor figure and AI organ visualizations achieved 15+ sec watch time. Key insight: creatives performed well, but post-click conversion was weak — funnel diagnosis, not creative problem.

ZenToes' Walmart campaign tested 10 different hook variations per format — each one a deliberate experiment in what stops a thumb in a foot care category. The modular system meant we could swap any component (hook, demo, CTA) without reshooting, generating dozens of testable combinations from 20 base assets. This is the testing velocity that separates brands that scale from brands that plateau.
OKAD Agency specializes in performance-driven video ad production for DTC brands, offering:
UGC video creation and editing with proven 8%+ view-to-25s retention
Hook testing and creative strategy (modular approach tested with ZenToes, Dadadababy, and alcohol brands)

Platform-specific optimization for TikTok, Meta, and YouTube
Ongoing creative iteration based on performance data

High-converting DTC video ads combine a strong hook, authentic storytelling, social proof, and a clear CTA. They are optimized for mobile viewing and tailored to platform-specific formats. OKAD Agency's campaigns consistently achieve 8%+ view-to-25-second retention by using modular hook testing and creator-led UGC — as proven by the ZenToes Walmart launch, Dadadababy's 3x CTR improvement with AI visuals under $700, Skribly's 1.5M views from 1,257 videos, and Twinsfit's 127K views from 485 followers.
For most platforms, 15-30 seconds performs best. TikTok and Reels favor 21-34 second videos, while YouTube allows longer formats for consideration-stage content.

TikTok and Instagram deliver the highest ROAS for most DTC categories, particularly for fashion, beauty, health, and consumer goods. A powerful pitch deck can make or break investor interest. Discover how OKAD Agency helped Trusto turn a complex product into a clear, compelling investor narrative. From bold visuals to strategic storytelling, learn how a well-designed deck boosted engagement, clarity—and investor confidence.
min reading
February 26, 2025

A well-structured pitch deck is a game-changer for startups looking to attract investors and secure funding. At OKAD Agency, we helped Trusto, a chargeback prevention startup, refine its investor presentation to make complex processes understandable and compelling. Here’s how we did it and what you can learn from our approach.
Investors don’t just invest in ideas; they invest in well-structured narratives. We ensured that each slide in Trusto’s pitch deck contributed to a cohesive and persuasive story.
Start with a strong problem statement: Highlight the pain point your product solves.
Introduce your solution: Make it clear and easy to grasp.
Present market potential: Show investors why this opportunity is worth their time.
Showcase your business model: Explain how your company generates revenue.
Provide financial projections: Use data to demonstrate growth potential.
End with a clear call to action: Tell investors what you need and why.
Data is powerful, but raw numbers can be overwhelming. We transformed Trusto’s financial and operational data into digestible visuals.
Used charts and infographics to highlight revenue potential and cost savings.
Created comparison tables to differentiate Trusto from competitors.
Highlighted key statistics with bold typography for easy scanning.
Your pitch deck’s design should reinforce trust and professionalism. For Trusto, we selected:
High-contrast fonts to emphasize key takeaways.
A palette of deep blues and soft neutrals to communicate reliability and technological innovation.
Custom icons and diagrams instead of generic stock images to explain processes effectively.
A pitch deck isn’t a research paper. Investors spend less than 4 minutes on average reviewing a deck, so every slide must be purposeful.
Keep text minimal – use bullet points, not paragraphs.
Limit slides to 10-12 for optimal engagement.
Use a clear and bold heading structure to guide the reader.
By combining strong messaging with a clean, visually engaging design, Trusto’s pitch deck became an effective tool for securing investor interest. The client reported:
Increased engagement from potential investors.
Positive feedback on the deck’s clarity and persuasiveness.
More confidence when presenting their solution.
A compelling pitch deck is an essential tool for any startup. If you’re looking to create a presentation that convinces and converts, consider these best practices. Need expert help?

A strong pitch deck should include a problem statement, solution, market opportunity, business model, financial projections, and a call to action. Each slide should build a compelling narrative for investors.
The ideal pitch deck is 10-12 slides long. Investors prefer concise presentations that quickly convey the most critical information.
Effective pitch decks use high-contrast typography, brand-aligned color palettes, clean layouts, and visual data representations to maintain engagement and readability.
Use data-driven estimates, industry benchmarks, and clear visual representations like charts and graphs to illustrate projected growth and revenue streams.
Avoid overloading slides with text, using too many slides, presenting unclear business models, and neglecting to define a clear call to action for investors.

UX issues can quietly kill conversion rates—especially for niche products. Discover how OKAD Agency tackled language barriers, user mistrust, and field interviews to improve Unistream Bank’s mobile app for migrants. Learn how smart UX research uncovered hidden friction and delivered fixes that boosted app performance and user satisfaction.
UX research
min reading
February 26, 2024

At OKAD Agency, we thrive on tackling complex challenges in user experience (UX) research. One of our most unique and demanding projects involved conducting UX research for Unistream Bank, a leading payment system for international money transfers.

This project required us to:✅ Find and interview respondents offline in challenging conditions✅ Overcome language barriers and user mistrust✅ Identify pain points in the banking app’s UX for migrants✅ Deliver actionable recommendations to improve conversion rates and user satisfaction

In Russia, major companies like Yandex and Sber have dedicated UX research teams, but niche products often struggle with usability testing. Many businesses assume that a well-designed interface guarantees success, but hidden UX issuescan lead to low conversion rates and user frustration.

Unistream’s team initially focused on improving their banking processes—office design, card processing algorithms, etc. However, negative user feedback persisted. That’s when they turned to us for an in-depth UX study of their mobile app.
Our mission was to analyze two core user flows in the Unistream banking app:1️⃣ Sending money abroad via phone number2️⃣ Sending money abroad via card number
By identifying common user mistakes and pain points, we aimed to increase transaction success rates and improve overall app usability.
We opted for qualitative interviews, which meant finding and speaking with real users offline—a challenging but necessary step.

🚧 Obstacles We Faced: ❄️ Extreme weather conditions made outdoor respondent searches difficult.🚫 Mistrust and data privacy concerns hindered participant willingness.🌍 Language barriers complicated interviews with migrants.
💡 Solution: We simplified research questions, ensured data anonymity, and Unistream provided a test build of the appto encourage participation.
🎯 Target respondents: Migrants who frequently use Unistream for international transfers, but who are not tech-savvyand struggle with app-based transactions.

🔹 Confusing sender data entry – Users mistakenly clicked "Change Data" when adding a document.🔹 Intimidating document selection – The variety of document types overwhelmed users.🔹 Unclear validation process – Errors (e.g., incorrect number/currency) only appeared at the end of the process.🔹 Format confusion – Users struggled with input fields, not realizing hyphens/spaces were required.

🔹 Recipient name confusion – Users often entered their own name instead of the recipient’s.🔹 First name/last name mix-up – Many users reversed these fields.🔹 Resetting selection errors – Re-selecting the transfer method automatically switched to cash pickup, erasing previous entries.
After analyzing user behavior, we systematized UX fixes based on priority and development effort:

✅ Quick Fixes (Low Effort, High Impact)✔ Add real-time validation to prevent incorrect entry submissions.✔ Provide tooltip explanations for document formats.✔ Introduce progressive disclosure (hiding less relevant document options until needed).

✅ Moderate Effort Fixes✔ Simplify UI copywriting for easier comprehension by non-native speakers.✔ Improve error messaging clarity (e.g., “Recipient name must match bank records”).✔ Allow auto-fill suggestions for frequently used details.

✅ Long-Term UX Improvements (Higher Effort)✔ Redesign flow to auto-save inputs, reducing accidental resets.✔ Implement localized versions of the app for different migrant communities.✔ Enhance onboarding tutorials to guide new users more effectively.

Thoroughly research your target market’s values, preferences, and lifestyles. Successful brands resonate deeply with their audiences' emotional and functional needs.
Clearly articulate how your fitness business uniquely meets your audience’s needs. Establish positioning statements highlighting your distinctive attributes and values.

In an increasingly competitive fitness market, brands must find unique ways to differentiate themselves. Jumpman, the first trampoline fitness studio in Paris, aimed to redefine its brand identity to stand out distinctly. Collaborating with OKAD Agency, they adopted an innovative theatrical branding approach to achieve this goal.

The "Phantom Stage, Elegance in Motion" concept transformed Jumpman’s brand from merely athletic to captivatingly theatrical. The idea was inspired by the stage, viewing trampolines as platforms where participants became performers, expressing themselves freely and energetically. This theatrical metaphor resonated deeply with Parisian culture, renowned for its artistic and performative heritage.

Previously, Jumpman featured a bulldog mascot, closely tied to the studio’s owner. OKAD Agency reimagined this mascot into an elegant phantom character reminiscent of "The Phantom of the Opera." Elements such as flowing capes, dramatic shadows, and spotlight effects emphasized the idea of movement and artistic expression. This playful yet sophisticated reinvention successfully connected emotional appeal with brand personality.

To complement the theatrical concept, OKAD Agency introduced dynamic gradients, intricate lighting effects, and dramatic color schemes. These elements vividly conveyed the theatrical essence and emotional depth of the brand. The strategic use of graphic elements like spotlight beams and gradient shadows created a cohesive visual narrative across all digital platforms and physical marketing materials.

The theatrical branding was seamlessly integrated into Jumpman’s new website, designed to attract both B2C and franchise-oriented B2B audiences. Fluid animations, interactive features, and compelling visual storytelling elements made the user experience engaging, memorable, and aligned with the theatrical positioning.
The comprehensive brand guidelines created in multiple languages facilitated consistent franchise growth, ensuring that all future studios retained the unique theatrical identity.

The theatrical branding approach significantly enhanced Jumpman’s market positioning in Paris. It resonated profoundly with the audience’s appreciation for creativity and performance, distinguishing the brand from conventional fitness studios. The reimagined mascot and consistent visual storytelling increased brand recall and emotional engagement, resulting in heightened interest from potential franchise partners.

A well-designed website is essential for businesses looking to effectively attract and engage both consumer (B2C) and business (B2B) audiences. An intuitive, visually appealing, and strategically structured website not only improves user experience but also enhances conversions. This article explores best practices in website design, illustrated through OKAD Agency’s successful Jumpman project.

A straightforward navigation structure helps both individual consumers and business visitors quickly find relevant content. Clearly differentiate sections for each audience, providing direct access to services, products, or franchise information.

Consistent visual branding builds credibility and improves brand recall. Utilize cohesive design elements, color schemes, and typography to ensure a seamless brand experience across all website pages.

Create distinct, audience-specific content areas. B2C content should emphasize immediate benefits, such as booking classes or memberships. B2B content should focus on long-term value propositions like franchise opportunities or partnerships.

Implement clear calls-to-action (CTAs) designed to guide visitors toward specific actions. For B2C, these might include straightforward booking buttons, while B2B CTAs could involve detailed contact forms or downloadable franchise guides.

OKAD Agency successfully applied these best practices to Jumpman's website redesign:
Navigation: Distinct sections were created, clearly separating class booking (B2C) from franchise opportunities (B2B).
Visual Identity: The theatrical visual style developed for Jumpman was consistently applied throughout, creating a memorable and engaging brand experience.
Content: The site featured targeted messaging for each audience type, clearly communicating benefits and opportunities.
Conversion Optimization: Clearly positioned CTAs were integrated into each page, enhancing user journeys and significantly improving conversion rates.
Interactivity: Interactive features and fluid animations vividly reflected Jumpman’s dynamic and performance-oriented brand identity.
Complex menus confuse visitors, negatively impacting user experience and conversions.

Generic calls-to-action can weaken user engagement and conversion effectiveness.
Solution: Craft specific, benefit-driven CTAs tailored explicitly to each audience segment.
Neglecting mobile responsiveness severely limits accessibility and user experience.
Solution: Prioritize responsive design, ensuring seamless functionality and consistent aesthetics across devices.
Clearly segment content for B2C and B2B audiences to optimize user journeys.
Maintain visual consistency to reinforce brand identity and credibility.
Strategically place engaging CTAs to maximize conversions.
Incorporate interactive elements for enhanced user engagement and memorability.

Jumpman, Paris's pioneering trampoline fitness studio since 2016, faced the challenge of redefining its brand identity and digital presence to support its expansion through franchising. They partnered with OKAD Agency, renowned for full-cycle marketing and branding services, to revitalize their brand, attract both B2C and B2B audiences, and position themselves distinctively on the French market.

Jumpman's original branding lacked the cohesive identity necessary for scalability and differentiation. The existing visual style and online presence didn't fully resonate with the vibrant and sophisticated expectations of Parisian consumers. Additionally, Jumpman needed a robust digital strategy to attract franchise partners and clearly communicate their unique business model.
OKAD Agency initiated the project by conducting extensive market research, audience analysis, and competitive audits to tailor Jumpman's new brand identity specifically for the French market.
Three innovative branding concepts were proposed:
Energy, Power in Motion: A bold, aggressive style inspired by sports and graffiti culture.
Neon Beats: An urban-centric visual style emphasizing neon aesthetics and social energy.
Phantom Stage, Elegance in Motion: A theatrical approach, using the trampoline as a metaphorical stage, creating a unique space for performance and self-expression.

The client embraced the Phantom Stage concept, highlighting theatrics and artistic flair. The existing mascot—a beloved bulldog—was transformed into a phantom-like character reminiscent of "The Phantom of the Opera," incorporating flowing capes, dramatic lighting, and dynamic gradients.
The website redesign featured:
An engaging UI/UX with fluid animations and interactive elements highlighting motion and energy.
Conversion optimization structures tailored separately for individual consumers (booking workouts) and franchise prospects.
A complex, visually appealing compositional grid reflecting the new theatrical brand identity.
Additional deliverables included bilingual brand guidelines, graphic assets for social media, and compelling franchise presentation materials.

The rebranding positioned Jumpman distinctly in the Paris fitness market, enhancing brand recognition and appeal. The refreshed visual identity successfully preserved cherished elements, particularly the mascot, while elevating the overall brand aesthetics. The new website effectively addressed both consumer and business needs, significantly improving user experience and engagement metrics.
Jumpman's franchising initiative received a robust strategic and visual framework, simplifying franchisee recruitment and onboarding processes.
Client feedback highlighted OKAD Agency's strategic vision, innovative design solutions, and the seamless execution that brought clarity and consistency to the Jumpman brand.

A dual-purpose website design enhances user experience and conversion rates for varied audiences.

Effective storytelling evokes emotions, making brands more relatable and memorable. The visuals should resonate deeply, reflecting the aspirations, experiences, or values of your audience.

Special attention was given to accessibility, ensuring the site appeals equally to tech-savvy youth and older generations familiar with classic navigation styles.

Since implementation, these interactive UX/UI features have significantly improved visitor engagement. The interactive map alone has notably increased the duration of user sessions, while the dynamic image gallery has encouraged deeper exploration of the venue's offerings. More importantly, these improvements have directly translated into increased ticket sales and enhanced user satisfaction.

Accessibility in web design isn’t merely a trend—it's essential to creating inclusive digital experiences. At OKAD Agency, when redesigning the website for a renowned creative venue in France, we prioritized accessibility to ensure every visitor, regardless of age or tech-savviness, could comfortably engage with the site. Here's how you can apply these valuable insights to your website.

Accessibility involves designing your website so all users, including older adults and those with varying degrees of digital literacy or impairments, can navigate and interact effortlessly. Good accessibility practices benefit all users, enhancing overall user satisfaction and engagement.

For the creative French venue, we simplified the menu structures, eliminating complicated dropdowns and confusing navigation paths. Clear, straightforward menus allow users of any age or technical ability to locate critical information without frustration.
Practical Tip: Keep menus intuitive, concise, and logical. Regularly test navigation ease with diverse user groups.

Choosing clear, legible fonts significantly improves readability, especially for older audiences or visually impaired users. After extensive testing, we selected fonts that were elegant yet easily readable on all devices.
Practical Tip: Select fonts with clear distinctions between characters, optimal spacing, and appropriate sizing to enhance readability.

A consistent layout builds familiarity, making navigation intuitive even for first-time visitors. By maintaining uniformity across pages, users can confidently navigate the site, understanding exactly where to find the content they seek.
Practical Tip: Use consistent header, footer, and sidebar structures throughout your website to create familiarity and ease of use.

Interactive elements, like buttons and links, should be clearly identifiable and easy to click or tap. Our redesign ensured all interactive elements were visually distinct, adequately sized, and appropriately spaced for comfortable interaction.
Practical Tip: Regularly test interactive elements for usability across various devices, ensuring easy access for all users.

Reducing cognitive load means minimizing unnecessary complexity in design and content. We carefully curated content to ensure clarity, avoiding overly technical language or excessive visuals that might overwhelm or confuse visitors.
Practical Tip: Focus on clarity in both visual design and textual content. Use straightforward language and simple visual structures to ensure comprehension.

Implementing these principles significantly enhanced the user experience of the French creative venue’s website, increasing engagement across all age groups and contributing to higher conversion rates and ticket sales.

Expanding your business internationally means navigating diverse technical and cultural landscapes. When Moboost, a data-driven advertising platform serving major global brands such as Adidas, HBO, and Binance, decided to expand their digital presence internationally, OKAD Agency helped them overcome the challenges with strategic website optimization. Here's your guide to effectively preparing and optimizing your website for global markets, inspired by our successful partnership with Moboost.

Local Hosting Solutions: To ensure reliable website performance, select hosting providers with infrastructure close to your target market. For Moboost, implementing local servers in strategic regions ensured fast load times and seamless access.
Optimize for Speed: Page load speeds are critical. Compress images, minify code, and leverage browser caching to improve user experience globally.
Ensure Accessibility: In restricted markets like China, ensure your website operates smoothly without the need for VPNs by conducting thorough testing and adjustments.

Cultural Relevance: Localization goes beyond translation; adapt your content to reflect cultural nuances and preferences of your target audience. Our content strategy for Moboost highlighted their key product benefits clearly and compellingly in each market.
SEO for Local Markets: Conduct market-specific keyword research to boost organic visibility and reach target audiences effectively.

Universal Design Principles: Implement clear navigation, intuitive interfaces, and accessibility features that accommodate diverse user preferences and technical abilities. Simplifying navigation for Moboost helped users from different markets effortlessly find essential information.
Responsive Design: Ensure your website adapts smoothly across all devices—desktop, tablet, and mobile. A responsive, consistent experience is crucial in maintaining engagement internationally.
User Testing: Engage local users for practical testing sessions to identify and correct any usability or technical issues early.
Performance Monitoring: Regularly track website performance metrics across different regions, continuously optimizing for improved user satisfaction and conversions.

Applying these strategies, Moboost successfully expanded their digital presence, dramatically improving website accessibility, user experience, and conversion rates internationally. Their optimized website performs seamlessly, catering effectively to users across diverse markets, including challenging regions like China.

Localization adapts content culturally and contextually, ensuring it resonates effectively with the target audience, whereas translation simply converts text from one language to another.

Responsive design ensures your site looks and performs consistently well across all devices, improving accessibility and user experience globally.

Regular, ideally monthly or quarterly, testing and performance analysis are recommended to maintain high standards and promptly address any emerging issues.

Pitch
min reading
April 14, 2025
Every startup dreams of securing investments, but here’s the catch: most never even get to the stage of creating a pitch deck, let alone sending it out to investors.

The Koster team came with an idea for a networking platform and needed a pitch deck to scale their project. We made it not only super stylish but also insanely effective — kept the vibe, added clear structure, numbers, and strong storytelling. In the end, it wasn't just about the product; investors could see these founders know how to lead and scale a team.

About the client: Koster is a unique service that combines group networking with dating to help people form meaningful connections. Unlike traditional dating apps, Koster focuses on creating lasting relationships by bringing people together in small, curated groups. The platform uses advanced algorithms to match users based on shared interests and values, providing them with an opportunity to form authentic friendships and connections over time.

About the task:The company had successfully developed an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) but was now at a pivotal stage — preparing to scale and attract investors. Koster needed a powerful investment pitch deck that would not only present their business model and growth potential but also reflect their distinctive approach to connection-building.

Koster had a strong concept, but the challenge was packaging that concept in a way that would resonate with investors. They needed a pitch deck that communicated their product’s value, market fit, and business potential clearly and concisely.

The primary issue was that the existing content was too complex, with long-winded explanations and a lack of visual appeal. The material didn’t align with the product’s sleek, modern design, and the narrative lacked structure. Koster needed more than just a traditional pitch deck; they needed a storytelling-driven presentation that would connect emotionally with potential investors and partners, while also showcasing the platform’s scalability and strong market fit.

At OKAD Agency, we specialize in crafting storytelling-driven pitch decks that not only convey critical business information but also engage and excite investors. To help Koster make an impact, we started by developing a clear narrative. Our goal was to bring out the emotional core of the brand — the desire to help people build meaningful relationships, not just quick matches.

We structured the pitch deck around storytelling principles that guided the flow of information and helped Koster stand out in the competitive dating and networking space. The following key points were included:
We clearly outlined the problem Koster was solving — the lack of authentic, long-term connections in traditional dating apps and the growing demand for meaningful, group-based networking experiences.

We emphasized the unique market opportunity for Koster at this moment in time. As social dynamics and dating preferences evolve, the demand for genuine, community-driven experiences has risen, making now the perfect time for Koster to scale.

Koster’s primary audience is young, urban professionals aged 23–40 who value connection, personal growth, and authenticity. The pitch deck provided a clear overview of their audience’s demographics and preferences.
We provided an overview of the dating and networking market, its current leaders, and trends, demonstrating that Koster is entering a growing space with significant potential.
By emphasizing Koster’s group-based, algorithm-driven matching system, we made sure investors understood how the product stood out and the advantages it offered over traditional platforms.

We explained Koster’s user experience, algorithms, and key product mechanics in a straightforward way. This included details on how the group-based model creates a more meaningful connection between users.
We clearly outlined Koster’s business model, including how they plan to generate revenue through premium subscriptions and features, and how their unit economics were structured for scalability.
The pitch deck included financial projections and a roadmap for scaling, providing investors with a clear understanding of the potential ROI and growth trajectory.

One of the most important elements of the Koster pitch deck was maintaining the brand’s unique style throughout the presentation. The design was fully aligned with the branding we had previously developed — sleek, modern, and emotionally engaging. We used Koster’s color palette, graphic patterns, and visual elements to ensure that the pitch deck felt like an extension of their product.

We also made the content visually digestible, using graphics and charts to break down complex information. Investors need to absorb key metrics quickly, so we focused on creating a design that emphasized clarity and simplicity while still making the presentation visually striking.

The final result was a pitch deck that Koster’s team could confidently use in meetings, emails, and negotiations. The deck was not just informative — it was emotionally engaging and visually compelling. By telling a clear, well-structured story, we helped Koster stand out in front of investors and partners, making their product and mission easy to understand and connect with.

Thanks to the storytelling-driven approach, the deck sparked immediate interest from early-stage investors. The visual emphasis on key metrics, combined with the compelling narrative, helped Koster effectively communicate their growth potential and vision.

A great product is only as strong as the way it is presented. When your pitch deck speaks the language of investors while still staying true to your brand, it becomes a powerful tool for growth. Koster’s pitch deck not only captured the essence of their mission but also provided investors with the clarity they needed to make a decision.

If you're preparing for investor meetings, a well-crafted pitch deck is crucial to communicate your startup’s potential. A compelling deck should present not only the problem you're solving and the uniqueness of your product, but also the financial viability, scalability, and market opportunity. Strong visual storytelling can help simplify complex ideas, ensuring your audience fully grasps your vision.

Marketing
min reading
April 21, 2025
In a world where every other brand is chasing followers and every third is after ad reach, it's not the one with the most likes who survives—it's the one who can turn attention into a system.

Cyber Pulse started as a niche car import service, helping clients bring vehicles from Germany to Portugal. Within a year, it had built strong trust and a loyal base of car lovers. Growth was steady — until it wasn’t. The Portuguese market was simply too small to scale further.

So, how do you grow when your product has hit a ceiling, but your audience is loyal and engaged?You build something bigger. That’s how Cybercore, a lifestyle car community, and Gently, a premium detailing studio, were born.

Many brands accumulate attention — followers, engagement, satisfied clients — but fail to activate it.Cyber Pulse had a goldmine: a passionate, engaged audience of car owners. But once they imported a car, there was no next step. Marketing ROI was declining. Growth had stalled. Something needed to change.

We designed a strategy that didn’t start with a new product. It started with people.We created a brand ecosystem, not just a rebrand. And we made sure it was built on real audience behavior, not assumptions.
Create a three-layer brand system:
Cyber Pulse remains the core service brand.
Cybercore becomes the cultural and community layer.
Gently offers the monetizable product (premium car detailing).
Develop visual identity and brand positioning for Gently:
Clean, premium, soft aesthetics.
Designed for both physical locations and digital presence.
Built to stand out in a competitive car services market.
Launch Cybercore as a real community:
Not just content, but real connection.
A name, a mission, a meeting space.
From test drives to car events — the brand became a lifestyle.
Organic audience migration and content strategy:
No paid ads, no spam.
Instead, strategic storytelling through Instagram and Telegram.
Cyber Pulse followers shifted into Cybercore naturally — and from there, into Gently as customers.
If you have clients, leads, or followers — you already have everything you need to launch a new brand.You just need to structure it correctly.
Listen to what your audience actually wants. Your next product might not be more of the same — it might be the next step in their journey.
Build community as an asset. Don’t treat engagement like a bonus — it’s your growth engine.
Create a brand ecosystem. Not just multiple brands, but a system that guides people from interest to purchase.
Go offline when possible. Physical spaces supercharge loyalty and visibility — especially in lifestyle or premium sectors.
Cybercore quickly became a lively platform for content, events, and car culture.
Gently launched with a warm customer pipeline already waiting — no cold start.
The three-brand system made it easy to build loyalty, community, and long-term monetization without aggressive sales.
Visual cohesion and storytelling created a strong, consistent brand presence both online and offline.
This case proves what modern brand builders are learning every day:People don’t just want products — they want to belong.
When you build for belonging, the conversion happens naturally.And if you don’t offer that experience, someone else will — and take your audience with them.

Why should I build a community if I already have clients?Because retention is cheaper than acquisition. A community strengthens trust, increases repeat business, and creates an organic referral engine.
Can I launch a second brand using the same audience?Absolutely — if you understand their evolving needs and position your new product as the next logical step in their journey.

Is community-led branding only for lifestyle or premium products?Not at all. Even in technical or B2B industries, a well-built community increases perceived value, thought leadership, and long-term customer engagement.

What if I don’t have a community yet?You can start building one from day one. We help clients identify their core audience, define the right narrative, and grow organically through content, spaces, and events.
Do I need a physical space to make this work?It helps — especially for trust and brand depth. But we’ve built strong digital-first communities too. The key is consistency, not real estate.

If your business is sitting on a loyal audience but struggling to grow, you're not out of options — you're sitting on your next brand.We help founders turn attention into action, build brand ecosystems, and grow without performance marketing addiction.

In B2B marketing, there’s one golden rule: if your offer doesn’t stop the scroll, you’re already dead. Brands that refuse to test, adapt, and produce native creatives fast enough don’t just fall behind — they vanish.

UpRest — a restaurant POS and back office software brand — was ready to launch in Portugal. They had a powerful product and a bold offer: free hardware, smart automation, and AI-powered food cost control.
But there was a problem.
They had no content.No validated messaging.No sales funnel.No understanding of how the Portuguese market would respond.
Their challenge was universal: how to enter a new market fast, build brand awareness, and generate high-quality leads — without wasting weeks and budget on guesswork.
Together, we defined four clear goals:
Launch in Portugal with a clear, localized value proposition
Test and validate offers to optimize for lowest cost per lead (CPL)
Build a lightweight but effective lead generation system from scratch
Scale with platform-native content on Meta and LinkedIn
We started with rapid market analysis, including:
Mapping the target audience: restaurant owners and managers
Identifying pain points (cost control, tech overwhelm, unreliable support)
Defining value pillars:
Free equipment
AI-based automation
Simple setup and onboarding
From there, we built offer hypotheses to test across formats and platforms.
With no existing content, we moved fast to build everything UpRest needed:
🧩 One-pager & pitch deck: for structured lead nurturing
🎯 Ad copy & offer variants: aligned with buyer pain points
🎥 Visuals, animations & AI-generated creatives
📲 Over 20 posts for Meta & LinkedIn: to fuel brand visibility
Everything was designed to be modular, testable, and scalable.
To reach our audience fast, we produced 20–30 second video ads with a mobile-first, story-driven approach:
Scripting via Google Sheets + Figma templates
Filming with phones for native social feel
Editing via CapCut Pro and Adobe AI for voice/audio polish
Output optimized for Meta Ads (Stories & Reels)
Time-to-publish for most assets: under 120 minutes.
We launched multiple campaign variations on Meta:
Testing different hooks, visuals, copy, and CTAs
Monitoring CPL, CTR, CVR daily

In the world of partnerships, the difference between “let’s talk” and radio silence often comes down to one thing: the deck.

Our client launched an educational initiative centered around French language learning through cultural immersion. The project already had a distinct voice — playful, visual, and human. But to take it further, they needed to scale partnerships with influencers, universities, and cultural organizations.
The problem? Their deck — the one tool meant to tell the story — simply wasn’t doing the job.
The first version of the presentation suffered from the three common problems we see with early-stage pitch decks:
Too much content, no clear narrative. It tried to say everything at once — and ended up saying nothing with impact.
Missing key information. Partner benefits were vague, the onboarding process wasn’t mapped, and there was no hierarchy of importance.
Visually inconsistent. The project’s charming identity wasn’t showing through, and the tone didn’t resonate with institutional partners.
The result: a deck that looked like a placeholder, not a partnership tool.
We kicked off with a deep dive: deconstructing the original content, identifying gaps, and realigning it with audience expectations.
What are we actually offering partners?
Why should they care — emotionally, strategically, financially?
What’s the flow from curiosity → credibility → conversion?
We rebuilt the entire story arc, starting with the essence of the project and ending with clear steps for collaboration.
We simplified without dumbing down:
Merged or split slides based on rhythm and attention span
Rewrote key headlines and body text for clarity and persuasion
Reorganized sections to guide different types of readers (creative, academic, executive)
Every slide had one job — and did it clearly.
While the brand had its own look, it lacked practical guidelines. We refined the visual identity and then applied it across the deck:
Updated typography and layout for legibility
Reworked illustrations and added contextual visuals
Balanced playful elements with a clean, serious structure for credibility
We also developed alternate versions of the deck tailored to different audiences: universities, influencers, media, and cultural institutions.
The final partner presentation became a go-to tool for outreach. It was:
Used in cold outreach, pitch meetings, and press discussions
Adapted quickly to different partners
Praised for its balance of charm and clarity
Instrumental in accelerating collaborations
Instead of getting ignored, the presentation sparked interest and structured the conversation.
Even when a product is brilliant, your deck needs to tell the story like it matters.
Here are 4 takeaways for anyone preparing a partner presentation:
Don’t write for yourself — write for the partner. What do they need to hear to say yes?
Simplify your message, not your value. Every slide should have one job, one emotion, one point.
Match tone to audience. A cultural product for institutions? Playful is fine — as long as the foundation is structured and credible.
Design is not decoration. It’s persuasion. It builds trust before you speak.

min reading
April 10, 2025

In a world where every media platform is screaming for attention, the ones that don’t invest in brand clarity are doomed to fade into noise. When your network looks like fifty unrelated side projects, no one takes your message seriously.

5Public is a rapidly growing network of 50 regional media outlets. Each operated independently — with its own logo, visual language, and content templates. While this setup worked at a small scale, it became a bottleneck as the brand grew.
The client came to us with three clear goals:
Build a unified visual identity across all 50 publications;
Make it scalable for non-designers and professionals alike;
Preserve the local identity of each city-based channel.
They had already tried to solve this internally, but the decentralized setup and lack of shared design standards made it impossible to align their look and feel across the board.
We started with research across the entire 5Public ecosystem:
Audit of all existing visual assets from different regions;
Competitive analysis of media brands with a national-local split;
Interviews with stakeholders to understand team workflows and platform limitations.
From this emerged a clear vision: a modular brand system, where each local media outlet retains a piece of its uniqueness, but fits into a broader, instantly recognizable identity.

The main breakthrough was the logo system. Rather than replacing the local character of each publication, we amplified it using map-based identifiers — each city’s outline became part of its official logo.
We paired this with:
A consistent font and layout system;
A color-coding scheme that helped visually organize regional identity;
Simplified logo variants and watermark versions for cross-platform use.
Design systems are only as good as their documentation. So we built an ecosystem of guides and toolkits to support daily use:
A full visual style guide, including typography, colors, logo use rules, and layout ratios;
Social media templates (15+ categories) for daily posts, news updates, carousels, and event coverage;
Instructions for working with low-quality imagery (a frequent challenge in fast-moving local news);
Assets optimized for both desktop and mobile editing, including Telegram and VK-specific formats.
We focused especially on enabling non-designers — local editors, marketers, and journalists — to work quickly and confidently inside a unified visual language.
A crucial part of brand unification is backend clarity. We:
Created 50 individual logo kits, organized by city;
Structured a Google Drive-based asset library, categorized by region and format;
Designed flexible templates that allow rapid adaptation with or without a designer;
Built a media kit template for use with sponsors and partners.
This system reduced bottlenecks, cut down on duplicate requests, and allowed instant onboarding of new regions or staff.
A unified yet flexible brand identity for 50 media channels;
Consistent look-and-feel across VK, Telegram, and internal documents;
Templates used daily by both professional designers and local content teams;
Seamless launch of the rebrand across all cities — completed in under 2 months;
Streamlined external communications with a ready-to-use media kit.
The client now has a scalable visual system that supports daily content creation, partnership outreach, and continued network expansion.
Don’t delay brand unification — fragmentation only worsens as your network grows.

Discover how targeted UX research and quick-win optimizations transformed Unistream Bank’s money transfer app for migrant users—eliminating form frustration, clarifying sender/recipient roles, and cutting task completion time without a full redesign. Learn actionable mobile app UX optimization strategies to boost conversions, reduce drop-offs, and elevate customer trust—read now!
UX research
min reading
April 8, 2025

In today’s digital world, ignoring user experience is like building a beautiful bridge without considering how people will actually cross it—eventually, everyone will turn around and find another way.

Unistream Bank, an international financial services provider, noticed significant user frustration with their money transfer mobile app, especially among migrant communities. Negative feedback indicated users struggled to complete essential tasks such as sending money transfers, uploading documents, and filling out forms correctly. To address these issues, a targeted UX research project was initiated to diagnose the precise usability pain points and propose practical, impactful improvements—without requiring a full application redesign.
Through detailed qualitative interviews and usability testing, our team identified several critical usability barriers impacting user experience:
Users failed to understand the purpose of certain buttons (like "Change data"), leading to confusion.
The excessive number of document types created anxiety and uncertainty during the verification process.
Errors in form validation appeared only after completing lengthy forms, frustrating users who had to redo processes multiple times.
Users regularly misunderstood whose personal information (sender or recipient) needed to be entered.
Names were often entered incorrectly (e.g., using Cyrillic instead of Latin characters or swapping first and last names).
Choosing a different transfer method caused previously entered information to reset, adding unnecessary friction and irritation.

To uncover these problems, our UX research team employed qualitative methodologies, including in-depth user interviews and structured testing sessions. The research process wasn't without challenges: participants were often skeptical, language barriers arose, and weather conditions sometimes impeded field research. Nevertheless, the comprehensive approach enabled us to capture authentic user interactions and reactions within real-life contexts, ensuring relevant and accurate data collection.

For effective UX research, it’s crucial to test real-world scenarios with diverse user groups. Particularly when targeting international and multilingual audiences, recognizing cultural nuances and language barriers significantly influences research outcomes and subsequent solutions.
Based on our findings, we proposed three tiers of recommendations to the bank—categorized according to implementation complexity:
Minor adjustments: Quick-win solutions with minimal code changes.
Moderate updates: Adjustments requiring slight modifications to app logic and user flows.
Critical priority: Fundamental issues urgently requiring attention for significant impact.
Among the most impactful recommendations implemented were:
Real-time validation: Errors and validation issues are now displayed immediately during data entry, reducing user frustration and abandonment rates.
Simplified document uploads: Clearer instructions and streamlined processes help users confidently select and upload required documents.
Distinct sender and receiver roles: Clear labels and step-by-step guidance minimize confusion, especially for first-time users.
Preservation of entered data: Preventing unnecessary resets when switching between payment methods significantly enhances user satisfaction and efficiency.
After the targeted UX optimizations were deployed, Unistream Bank observed measurable improvements, including:
A notable decrease in incomplete transaction rates.
Increased user trust and confidence in the app.
Enhanced efficiency, reducing the overall time needed to complete transactions.
These improvements not only directly enhanced the user experience but also positively influenced the bank’s brand perception among migrant communities.

This case underscores the substantial impact achievable through focused UX research and incremental improvements. Companies don’t always need full redesigns to achieve better results—well-targeted, research-driven adjustments often deliver powerful outcomes.
Targeted UX research can uncover subtle yet significant usability issues.
Simple, incremental UX improvements often provide immediate and substantial benefits.
Understanding the specific needs and challenges of your audience is critical, especially when dealing with diverse or international user bases.
Prioritizing UX enhancements based on impact and feasibility can deliver impressive results with limited resources.
If your users are frustrated and your app or website struggles with retention, we can help identify precise UX problems and provide actionable solutions quickly.
Let’s discuss your UX challenges together https://tally.so/r/3jElgx

What is UX research, and why is it important?UX research involves studying user behavior to improve digital products. It’s essential because a poor user experience often directly translates into lost revenue and customer dissatisfaction.

How quickly can UX improvements show results?Significant improvements can appear within weeks after implementing targeted UX recommendations, especially if these enhancements directly address critical user pain points.

How do you recruit participants for UX research when the target audience is hard to reach?We combine community outreach, social‑media micro‑targeting, and on‑the‑ground intercepts. When language or trust barriers exist (e.g., among migrant users), we employ bilingual screeners and offer session formats that feel safe and convenient for participants.

What’s the typical time‑frame for a focused UX study and quick‑win rollout?A lean, problem‑specific study—including recruitment, interviews, analysis, and prioritized recommendations—usually takes 3–5 weeks. High‑impact fixes can go live immediately after, often within the same quarter.

Do UX improvements always require code releases?Not necessarily. Many pain points can be resolved with copy tweaks, micro‑interaction adjustments, or clearer in‑app instructions—changes that design or product teams can ship without a full development cycle.

How do you measure ROI on UX fixes?We track task‑completion rates, drop‑off points, and support‑ticket volumes before and after each change. For financial apps, metrics such as completed transfers, average transaction value, and session time provide clear ROI signals.

Can we run UX research remotely if our users are spread across countries?Yes. We use moderated video sessions, unmoderated tasks, and remote diary studies. For sensitive cohorts, we add local community facilitators to ensure cultural alignment and richer insights.

What if we plan a full redesign later—should we still invest in smaller UX fixes now?Absolutely. Quick wins relieve immediate friction, boost user trust, and provide validated insights that de‑risk the larger redesign. Think of them as stepping‑stones rather than sunk effort.

Light-filled gradients, smooth animations, and soft edge interactions

Thoughtful typography and layout for accessibility and calmness
This is not just interface—it’s immersive visual care.
To support growth and acquisition, we designed the marketing site with:
Clear brand-aligned messaging about the app’s benefits
Trust-building design based on user psychology
Flexible landing structure that can support future A/B testing and content campaigns
Your product’s first point of contact is your website—so it has to work just as hard.
One year after launch, the Samto team returned for help improving the app. We:
Analyzed behavioral data from early users
Improved navigation and added new user-requested features

min reading
April 25, 2025
If your product is hard to use, people won’t just drop off — they’ll flee.

In technical industries like property evaluation or mortgage processing, users don’t have time—or patience—for clunky interfaces. When a process is already stressful (like getting a home loan), every confusing step feels like a dealbreaker. A bad dashboard doesn't just delay decisions — it loses customers. Platforms that fail to simplify complexity will quickly be replaced by those that do. In a service category where reports are mandatory and time-sensitive, usability isn’t a luxury. It’s the entire business model.

Ocenka RF is a real estate evaluation service focused on clients applying for mortgages and professionals needing certified valuation reports. The client came to us after a failed attempt by a previous agency, looking for a fast and effective redesign of their portal and personal account system. The stakes were high: they needed something live and functional in a matter of weeks.
Our mission was to build a modern UX/UI system that made it easy for users to:
Submit property data
Receive detailed reports
Track their evaluation status
Navigate across devices without frustration
We delivered a fully functional design in just 2 weeks, while also elevating the brand’s digital perception.
Tight deadlinesThe client had a strict go-live timeline. We worked in agile sprints with rapid feedback loops, simultaneously designing for desktop, tablet, and mobile.
Visually dry contentThe core product was a 40-page property evaluation report. Presenting it in an appealing way was critical to avoid user fatigue.
Confusing UX for multiple audiencesThere were two main user groups—those ordering evaluations, and those tracking mortgage reports. Both needed clear paths with minimal overlap.
The homepage uses tabs to let users quickly identify their path: "For Individuals" vs. "For Mortgage Clients". This simple UX pattern drastically reduces cognitive load from the start.
Instead of showcasing long, text-heavy documents, we built the interface around custom illustrations that visualize key steps and reassure users.
We kept the interface clean—white space, intuitive spacing, soft transitions—and used microanimations to communicate states (loading, success, error) without overwhelming the user.
The portal was built with full responsiveness in mind. We designed for all three screen types (desktop, tablet, mobile) from the beginning, ensuring consistent experiences everywhere.
Though this was a client-facing product, we made sure that the backend team could easily update report statuses, trigger notifications, and access user data from a clean, internal layout.
Delivery within 2 weeks, including all key flows and responsive versions
Intuitive dashboard that reduced customer support inquiries

Flip System is a CRM platform built for real estate professionals flipping, renting, or selling properties. They approached us with a clear challenge: produce a large-scale series of performance-driven creatives that not only drive results but also uphold a strong, flexible brand identity across platforms.

We were tasked with developing both static and motion content for paid campaigns — content that could engage, educate, and convert. This meant clarity, speed, visual consistency, and a whole lot of iteration.
Develop a high-volume package of graphics for paid campaigns.
Produce motion creatives that communicate product value quickly and clearly.
Maintain brand consistency while introducing stylistic variety.

From there, we built over 100+ ad variations — experimenting with layout, typography scale, and illustration styles — all using the same copy. This made A/B testing efficient and meaningful.

Created multiple design systems based on one value prop.
Applied “design remixing” — one core idea rendered in different styles.
Used known visual triggers from the real estate niche (floor plans, keys, dashboards, etc.).

Built scenes that mirrored the real user experience.
Introduced soft motion transitions for scroll-friendly feeds.
Used animated UI walkthroughs to mimic in-product interaction.

With the launch of their new location in Vienna, Austria, they faced the challenge of promoting their courses locally without a physical presence. We were tasked with creating a strategic approach to social media marketing and targeted advertising, aiming to engage both local parents and kids interested in technology and robotics education.

The goal was simple but crucial: attract families to enroll their children in Robbo's courses, particularly in programs like Lego Robotics, Minecraft Modding, and coding courses. Our efforts to optimize Robbo’s social media profiles led to a noticeable improvement in their overall visual and informational quality. Parents now had an easier time understanding the value of the courses, which significantly contributed to a positive shift in brand perception.

A strategic approach to content marketing, tailored to the specifics of each educational track (Lego, Minecraft, and coding courses), ensured effective engagement with diverse audiences, even in a remote setting.

min reading
